More details below Z Encryption via KRYPTOS Vigenene Encryption Step 2 Result of Step 1 Previous Ciphertext (starts 2 characters behind, then changes to 3) Encryption via KRYPTOS Vigenene - Final Result K4 Ciphertext Delta between resulting CT and Kryptos K4 expressed as a letter (K=0) Lag changes from 2 characters to 3 characters resulting in "UU" (coincidence or hinted at by UNDERGR UU ND?) Aperiodic Key? I don't what causes it to move to the next section Key for step 1? Spaced to show similarities between first half and second half of K4. H & Q created in PT by changing S O LI to S U LI Using key UV instead of VW This just seems to work better with a CT of NY YT TT instead of NY PV TT Character # Step 1 Key Decryption Step 1 CT Proposed K4 Decryption Method Decryption via KRYPTOS Vigenene Decryption Step 2 Decryption via KRYPTOS Vigenene - Final Result Aperiodic Key? Explanation on Encryption tab Tried different letters here. HW (from the end of K3 CT) is an alternative, but requires a key letter of G for the first step to produce T. I've tried to get the keys for the first and second half to match by adjusting letters of the PT, but I keep ending up here. Numerical equivalent of key (KRYPTOS alphabet) More details on Encryption tab S requires a key letter of G Occurs at key shift. Using O instead of K results in an S. Reads similarly, CLOCKES vs. CLOCKSS Occurs at key shift. Using A instead of R results in an O. WW Hero in Berlin? PANEL and PAPER both seem to require at least one out of sequence key letter. Interesting Alternatives Uses end of K3 as primer (coincidence similar to LAYERTWO & IDBYROWS?) I do not know how this would have been generated, but I'm content with the pattern and similarities between the first and second halves. CTAK Key (Offset 2) Decrypt via Kryptos Vigenere CTAK Key (Offset 3) Extend Kryptos alphabet Could vary based on the notes above, grouped in an attempt to make sense of it
